`eslint-disable` comments are JavaScript comments, so in a component they only work in the scripts and the template expressions. With this rule and eslint-plugin-svelte's processor, HTML comments in the markup work too: `<!-- eslint-disable -->`, `<!-- eslint-enable -->`, `<!-- eslint-disable-line -->` and `<!-- eslint-disable-next-line -->`, each with or without rule names and with an optional `-- reason`. An `<!-- eslint-disable -->` ends where the next `<script>` starts.

What such a comment disables is removed from the results. Unlike what a JavaScript comment disables, it isn't listed as suppressed.

It needs the processor of `eslint-plugin-svelte`, `processor: "svelte/svelte"`: without it the rule does nothing.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. It runs on the Svelte components that an ESLint config lints with `svelte-eslint-parser`, in the place of the rule of `eslint-plugin-svelte`:

{/* skip */}

```js eslint.config.js
import svelte from "eslint-plugin-svelte";

export default [
  ...svelte.configs.recommended,
  { rules: { "svelte/comment-directive": "error" } },
];
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

With the processor, nothing is reported here:

{/* good {"processor": true} */}

```svelte
<!-- eslint-disable-next-line svelte/no-at-html-tags -- the text is sanitized -->
{@html description}
```

## Options

| Option                          | Default | What it does                                                                   |
| ------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `reportUnusedDisableDirectives` | `false` | Report an HTML comment that disables or enables nothing, as an unused directive |

Reported with `{ "reportUnusedDisableDirectives": true }`, because `<p>` has nothing to disable:

{/* bad {"processor": true, "options": [{"reportUnusedDisableDirectives": true}]} */}

```svelte
<!-- eslint-disable-next-line svelte/no-at-html-tags -->
<p>{description}</p>
```
